{"id": "5b1c18e1-e12f-4a72-8e57-3d6d6b9afb1f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Switching takes one setting change and causes no application downtime. I found no EFS file systems in us-east-1 for account 012345678901_1, so I couldn't check which mode yours is on.

**How to switch**

- **Console:** Open the file system in the EFS console and choose **Edit**. Under **Throughput mode**, select **Enhanced → Elastic** and save.
- **AWS CLI:**
  ```
  aws efs update-file-system \
    --file-system-id fs-xxxxxxxx \
    --throughput-mode elastic \
    --region <region>
  ```
  You don't set a throughput amount. Elastic scales with your workload, and any provisioned amount is dropped.

**Before you switch**

- **Provisioned mode:** If you changed to Provisioned or raised the provisioned amount in the last 24 hours, you can't switch to Elastic until that window ends.
- **Bursting mode:** If the file system is on Bursting, you can switch right away.
- **Cost:** Elastic bills per GB of data read and written instead of for provisioned or burst capacity. Set a CloudWatch alarm on `MeteredIOBytes` so a busy workload doesn't surprise you on the bill.
- **Possible other causes:** If throughput is low while the mode is already Elastic, the cause is probably somewhere else. Check the Max I/O performance mode, client count and thread parallelism, mount options (use the EFS mount helper), and network limits on the instance.

If the file system is in another region or account, tell me which one and I'll check its current mode and throughput metrics. I can also run the change for you once you confirm the file system ID. It needs your approval before it runs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
